evidence.quote: if incoming data suggest that inflation is more persistent than I currently expect it to be, it will be appropriate to hold in place the current restrictive stance of policy for longer.
While we have seen considerable progress in lowering inflation, the job of sustainably restoring 2 percent inflation is not yet done.
Recent readings on both job gains and inflation have come in higher than expected.
My baseline outlook continues to be that inflation will decline further, with the policy rate held steady at its current level
I am fully committed to getting inflation back to 2 percent.

parsed.rationale: Mostly a historical speech on uncertainty, but the current-situation section notes higher-than-expected job and inflation readings, a baseline of rates held steady, and possibly holding restrictive policy longer, with no mention of cuts. This is a moderate hawkish lean.
